_comment: Each entry supplies OVERRIDES ONLY. Any assumption not listed keeps its
base-case value. Unknown assumption keys are rejected rather than ignored.
'add_ons' is optional; omit it to keep the blueprint add-on schedule, or
supply [] to model the platform with no tuck-ins.
These cases are author-defined illustrations, not blueprint scenarios.
The shipped 'downside' scenario in buy_and_build_model.py remains the
blueprint's IC guardrail case and is not changed by anything here.

scenarios.name: severe-downside
scenarios.description: Underwriting stress case: overpay at entry, normalization fails, revenue declines 3% a year, add-on programme partly fails, credit tightens, and the exit re-rates down.
scenarios.source: Author-defined severe downside. NOT the blueprint downside. Built because the blueprint IC guardrail case varies only growth, synergy capture, interest, and the exit mark, and still returns 3.58x, exploring a narrow band of outcomes. This is a modeled capital-impairment case, not a guaranteed lower bound: worse outcomes remain possible.

_stress_rationale.platform_entry_multiple: 6.0x -> 7.0x. Competitive process; we bid up to win.
_stress_rationale.platform_ebitda_margin: 20% -> 16.5%. Owner add-backs did not hold and prevailing-wage exposure was understated at diligence.
_stress_rationale.platform_margin_expansion_bps_per_year: 50 -> 0. The operational improvement thesis does not land.
_stress_rationale.annual_organic_growth: +5% -> -3%. Loss of a major municipal contract plus budget deferrals across the base. Modelled as post-close decline rather than a smaller platform at entry. Under this model's construction — fixed absolute add-on sizes and an unchanged entry multiple — shrinking the platform raises modeled MOIC, because the lower-multiple add-ons contribute a larger share of a smaller deal. That is an artefact of those held-constant inputs, not a general finding that smaller platforms return more.
_stress_rationale.sgna_synergy_capture: 15% -> 5%, realization 50% -> 25%. Integration takes longer and delivers less.
_stress_rationale.interest_rate: 8.0% -> 10.5%. Credit conditions tighten as performance deteriorates.
_stress_rationale.terminal_multiple: 6.5x -> 5.0x. A shrinking, lower-margin platform does not earn a scaled-platform re-rating.
_stress_rationale.add_ons: Add-on A closes but underperforms its margin case (18% -> 13%); Add-on B closes a year late and smaller; Add-on C never closes.

scenarios.name: integration-failure
scenarios.description: Isolates add-on execution risk: the platform performs to the base case, but the tuck-in programme underdelivers.
scenarios.source: Author-defined single-driver case. The blueprint downside cannot express this at all, because it varies only assumption rates and never the acquisition schedule.

_stress_rationale.add_ons: Same failed programme as severe-downside, with every platform assumption left at base. Isolating the driver shows how much of the return depends on tuck-ins actually closing and hitting their case.

scenarios.name: revenue-decline
scenarios.description: Municipal budgets tighten: revenue shrinks 2% a year, synergies half-captured, 9.5% interest, 5.5x exit mark.
scenarios.source: Author-defined illustration. Not specified in PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md.

scenarios.name: credit-stress
scenarios.description: No tuck-ins and expensive debt: platform only, 12% interest, flat growth.
scenarios.source: Author-defined illustration. Not specified in PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md.

scenarios.name: lender-credits-synergies
scenarios.description: Tests the financing governor when a lender credits the full synergy add-back at a 2.5x ceiling.
scenarios.source: Author-defined illustration. Lender treatment is not a covenant term.
